title: Review: Maxwell–Boltzmann and catalysts; Measuring rates; Dynamic equilibrium and Kc expressions
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: KN01#t1 term and clue written for the game; KN03#t1 term and clue written for the game; KN03#t2 term and clue written for the game; KN01#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EQ01#N.6, KN01#N.8a, KN03#N.3a, EQ01#N.8a, KN01#N.3a, KN03#N.12, EQ01#N.3a, EQ01#N.10a, EQ01#N.13, EQ01#N.12. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Rate of reaction
items.clue: Change in the concentration of a substance per unit time, quoted as a positive value.

items.label: Activation energy
items.clue: On a profile, the height from the reactants up to the top of the barrier; always positive.

items.label: Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution
items.clue: Curve of number of molecules against energy: starts at the origin, peaks, has a long tail.

items.label: Tangent
items.clue: A straight line drawn at one time on the curve; its gradient gives the rate at that instant.

questions.stem: Which is the equilibrium constant expression for 4NH₃(g) + 5O₂(g) ⇌ 4NO(g) + 6H₂O(g)?

options.text: Kc = [NO]⁴[H₂O]⁶ / ([NH₃]⁴[O₂]⁵)
Kc = [NO]⁴ / ([NH₃]⁴[O₂]⁵)
Kc = [NH₃]⁴[O₂]⁵ / ([NO]⁴[H₂O]⁶)

questions.explanation: Products over reactants, each raised to the power of its coefficient. All four species are gases, so H₂O(g) is included.

questions.stem: A student reacts 0.10 g of magnesium ribbon with excess dilute hydrochloric acid: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). Which method is least suitable for measuring the rate of this reaction?

options.text: Collecting the hydrogen in a gas syringe and reading the volume every 10 s
Recording the loss in mass of the flask on a balance every 10 s
Taking samples at timed intervals, quenching them and titrating the acid left
Timing how long it takes to collect the first 20 cm³ of hydrogen in a gas syringe

questions.explanation: H₂ has a tiny molar mass: 0.10 g of Mg gives only about 0.008 g of H₂. A typical balance can barely detect the total loss, let alone the changes between readings.

questions.stem: Which energy profile correctly shows an endothermic reaction?

options.text: Products higher than reactants; Ea arrow from the reactants up to the peak; ΔH arrow from reactants up to products.
Products higher than reactants; Ea arrow from the products up to the peak.
Products lower than reactants; ΔH arrow pointing down; Ea arrow from reactants up to the peak.
Products higher than reactants; Ea arrow from the reactants up to the products level.

questions.explanation: Endothermic means products are higher in energy. Ea runs from the reactants to the top of the barrier; ΔH from reactants to products.

questions.stem: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g). At equilibrium, [N₂] = 0.50, [H₂] = 0.40 and [NH₃] = 0.30 mol dm⁻³. What is Kc?

options.text: 0.36 mol² dm⁻⁶
1.5 dm³ mol⁻¹
2.8 dm⁶ mol⁻²
2.8 mol² dm⁻⁶

questions.explanation: Kc = 0.30² ÷ (0.50 × 0.40³) = 0.090 ÷ 0.032 = 2.8. Units: (mol dm⁻³)² ÷ (mol dm⁻³)⁴ = (mol dm⁻³)⁻² = dm⁶ mol⁻².

questions.stem: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes: 2H₂O₂(aq) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g). Which quantity is the rate of this reaction at a particular moment?

options.text: The total time taken for all of the H₂O₂ in the sample to decompose
The total volume of O₂ given off by the time the reaction has stopped
The decrease in the concentration of H₂O₂ per unit time at that moment
The concentration of H₂O₂ at that moment divided by the time elapsed so far

questions.explanation: Rate is the change in concentration per unit time, in mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. At a moment, it is the gradient of the tangent, quoted as positive.

questions.stem: A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen can stay unchanged at room temperature for years. In Döbereiner's lamp (1823), a jet of hydrogen in air strikes a piece of platinum and reacts at once, with no flame or spark to start it. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The platinum heats the gas, so the curve moves to higher energy and more molecules exceed the same Ea.
The platinum gives a route with a lower Ea, so at the same temperature far more molecules have enough energy.
The platinum makes the reaction more exothermic, so the molecules gain the energy they need to react.
The platinum changes the shape of the curve, moving its peak to higher energy without heating.

questions.stem: Hydrogen and iodine are heated in a sealed flask at constant temperature until the amount of hydrogen iodide no longer changes: H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g). Which statement must be true of the mixture at this point?

options.text: No HI forms or decomposes now, as both reactions have stopped.
HI forms and decomposes at equal rates, so its amount stays the same.
The concentrations of H₂, I₂ and HI have become equal to each other.
Half of the hydrogen and iodine has been converted into hydrogen iodide.

questions.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium: in the closed flask both reactions continue at equal rates, so the concentrations of H₂, I₂ and HI stay constant.

questions.stem: For the reaction X(g) ⇌ Y(g), K = 1.0 × 10¹⁵ at 298 K. Which statement about this reaction at 298 K is correct?

options.text: At equilibrium, the mixture is made up almost entirely of X.
At equilibrium, almost all of X has been converted into Y.
At equilibrium, X and Y are present in similar amounts.
The large value of K shows that equilibrium is reached quickly.

questions.explanation: K ≫ 1, so [Y]/[X] = 1.0 × 10¹⁵: the position lies far to the right and the reaction goes almost to completion.

questions.stem: A mixture of hydrogen and chlorine can be kept in the dark for days with no visible change. Yet for H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) ⇌ 2HCl(g), K ≈ 2 × 10³³ at 298 K. What do these facts tell you?

options.text: At equilibrium it would be mostly H₂ and Cl₂, because no HCl forms in the dark.
It is already at equilibrium, because nothing changes while it is in the dark.
At equilibrium it would be almost all HCl; in the dark it reacts extremely slowly.
It must react quickly in the dark, because a very large K means a fast reaction.

questions.explanation: K ≫ 1, so the equilibrium lies far to the right. K tells you how far, not how fast: in the dark the reaction is too slow to see.

questions.stem: CO₂(g) + H₂(g) ⇌ CO(g) + H₂O(g). The forward reaction is endothermic. Which change increases the value of Kc?

options.text: Adding more H₂ at constant temperature
Raising the pressure at constant temperature
Adding a catalyst
Raising the temperature

questions.explanation: Only temperature changes Kc. The forward reaction is endothermic, so Kc increases as the temperature rises.
